tasks_completed.description: F1: single-snapshot + self-kill guard + PID liveness check in stopDaemon()
tasks_completed.changes: stopDaemon() now reads state.json exactly once into 'state'. Added self-kill guard (state.pid === process.pid). Added PID liveness check (process.kill(state.pid, 0)) using cached state — no second read. Replaced stopDaemonHttp() / daemonPost() call with inline fetch to state.httpPort — eliminates the second independent read of state.json that caused the split-target race. SIGKILL fallback uses state.pid from same snapshot. Log message improved: 'Graceful stop did not complete' instead of 'HTTP stop failed' for clarity.
tasks_completed.rationale: Root cause: daemonPost() re-read state.json independently at line 15 for HTTP port while stopDaemon() captured PID at line 198 — creating a window where HTTP stop and SIGKILL could target different daemon generations. Fix: single snapshot eliminates the window.

tasks_completed.description: Remove lock file deletion block from clearDaemonState() in persistence.ts (F2a)
tasks_completed.changes: Removed the 'if (existsSync(configuration.daemonLockFile)) { try { await unlink(daemonLockFile) } catch {} }' block (7 lines). Updated JSDoc from 'Clean up daemon state file and lock file' to 'Clean up daemon state file only. Lock file lifecycle is owned exclusively by acquireDaemonLock / releaseDaemonLock.' (2 lines added). Net: -7 lines.
tasks_completed.rationale: clearDaemonState() was deleting the lock file it does not own. The lock lifecycle belongs exclusively to acquireDaemonLock / releaseDaemonLock. Stale lock cleanup is already handled by acquireDaemonLock's retry loop at line 364.

tasks_completed.description: Confirmed releaseDaemonLock() already handles ENOENT via catch {} — no code change needed (AC5)
tasks_completed.changes: Read releaseDaemonLock() at persistence.ts:379-389. Both the lockHandle.close() and the unlinkSync() are wrapped in independent try { } catch { } blocks that silently swallow all errors including ENOENT. No code change required.
tasks_completed.rationale: AC5 requires ENOENT to be silently swallowed. The existing catch {} is already sufficient.

tasks_completed.description: Fix cleanup order at Site 1 (heartbeat handoff ~line 763-767): releaseDaemonLock before cleanupDaemonState
tasks_completed.changes: Swapped releaseDaemonLock(daemonLockHandle) to appear before cleanupDaemonState() in the bundleReplaced heartbeat handoff block
tasks_completed.rationale: Lock must be released before state file is deleted; otherwise a new daemon that acquires the lock and reads state.json may find stale data, or releaseDaemonLock may attempt to unlink a file already deleted by clearDaemonState — root cause commit ed4b15bb8

tasks_completed.changes: Swapped releaseDaemonLock(daemonLockHandle) to appear before cleanupDaemonState() in cleanupAndShutdown function
tasks_completed.rationale: Same lock lifecycle ordering principle — lock must be released before state file is deleted; stopCaffeinate moved after cleanupDaemonState (was already last)

tasks_completed.description: Fix F3: move process.exit(0) inside try block; add process.exit(1) in catch block with FATAL log
tasks_completed.changes: process.exit(0) moved to inside try block immediately after successful spawnHappyCLI call; catch block now emits FATAL log then calls process.exit(1) instead of continuing; removed unconditional process.exit(0) that was outside try block
tasks_completed.rationale: After full teardown (apiMachine, controlServer, state, lock, caffeinate), a failed spawn leaves zero subsystems — the daemon has no control path. process.exit(1) allows systemd Restart=on-failure to respawn. Prior unconditional exit(0) suppressed supervisor respawn signal.
